source_title: Privacy and Personal Information Protection Act 1998 No 133
evidence_description: Section 27 of the PPIP Act provides a specific exemption from information protection principles for NSW Police Force, with principles applying in connection with administrative and educative functions.
investigation_relevance: Defines baseline statutory privacy framework and police-specific exception; does not prove any particular surveillance practice.

source_title: Guide to undertaking Privacy Impact Assessments on AI systems and projects
evidence_description: NSW IPC AI privacy-impact guidance states contracted vendor access solely for an agency service may be treated as agency use rather than disclosure; other external access may constitute disclosure, depending on facts.
investigation_relevance: Directly qualifies whether contractor access is a use or disclosure, countering overbroad assumptions.

source_title: Guide to section 121 of the GIPA Act for private sector contractors (July 2026)
evidence_description: NSW IPC July 2026 guidance explains GIPA s 121 contractual immediate-access provisions apply to private contractors providing services to the public on behalf of NSW agencies; applicability to specific police IT contracts requires separate verification.
investigation_relevance: Defines conditional contractor transparency mechanism and scope limit.

source_title: Fact Sheet - Local councils' use of CCTV cameras in public places
evidence_description: NSW IPC guidance distinguishes local-council CCTV filming in public places from privately owned land and states the council-specific regulation exemption does not extend to private-land cameras.
investigation_relevance: Prevents incorrect application of council CCTV provisions to hypothetical hotel cameras.

source_title: Fact Sheet - Managing access to audio visual information under the GIPA Act
evidence_description: NSW IPC guidance explains GIPA access pathways for audiovisual records and identifies third-party personal information as a relevant public-interest consideration.
investigation_relevance: Establishes access-rights and privacy-balancing inquiry for police-held footage.

source_title: Guide to undertaking Privacy Impact Assessments on AI systems and projects
hash_exception_reason: Primary web text independently reviewed; original source file not yet preserved in case repository.
evidence_description: IPC guidance explicitly identifies AI systems that process CCTV and vehicle-registration data, and states that PIAs for AI handling personal information are ordinarily risk-based and typically required. This establishes regulatory guidance, not actual NSW deployment.
relevant_quotation: If an AI system or project involves handling personal information, a PIA will typically be required.
investigation_relevance: Establishes an official baseline for investigating AI/CCTV data flows, third-party disclosures and privacy assessment controls; applicability to a particular deployment requires separate evidence.

evidence_description: The NSW AI Assessment Framework publication is registered as official NSW Government guidance concerning agency AI assurance.
NSW Government guidance addresses identification of AI use in agency systems.
NSW Department of Customer Service published an announcement concerning modernised AI oversight.

source_title: National Framework for Assurance of AI
evidence_description: IPC NSW published material concerning the national AI assurance framework.
The registered IPC NSW guide catalogue requires document-level identification before specific propositions are attributed.
An official IPC NSW privacy impact assessment PDF has an archived source copy and SHA-256 recorded in the source register.
Official NSW Digital NSW publication concerning AI assessment and governance. Specific obligations and effective dates require passage-level validation before application to an agency.
investigation_relevance: Establishes a government AI assessment source for subsequent deployment-specific compliance checks.

source_title: NSW IPC AI Privacy Impact Assessment Guide
evidence_description: A PDF copy of NSW IPC guidance on privacy impact assessments for AI systems is preserved in the source archive and linked by recorded SHA-256. Passage-level examination and applicability remain separate verification steps.
investigation_relevance: Preserved primary regulatory guidance for AI privacy risk and CCTV-related inquiries.

evidence_description: The NSW AI Assessment Framework states that the AIAF Platform is mandatory from 30 September 2026 for registration of NSW Government AI use cases. High and critical risk cases receive additional review.
NSW guidance on identifying AI instructs agencies to register solutions that use or may use AI, and to document determinations that AI is not used, with review when features or use changes.

The NSW Department of Customer Service announcement describes privacy impact assessment, cyber security and legal review, and AI Review Committee oversight in an illustrative high-risk AI chatbot case. This example does not establish surveillance deployment.

NSW IPC November 2024 guidance treats identifiable council CCTV recordings as personal information. It discusses conditional exemptions for CCTV in public places, including live transfer to NSW Police, and limits concerning privately owned land.

The IPC fact sheet describes PPIP Regulation exemptions relevant to public-place council CCTV and live transmission to NSW Police. Scope and applicability to any identified installation remain unverified.

The July 2026 NSW IPC fact sheet states that GIPA Act section 121 requires certain public service contracts with private sector entities to give agencies immediate access to specified contractor-held information, subject to statutory exceptions.
verification_state: Archived official source text reviewed; applicability to specific contracts unverified

evidence_description: The NSW IPC July 2026 fact sheet describes audiovisual records including CCTV, body-camera, dashcam and drone footage as government information when held by agencies. It addresses records management, retention and access under applicable legislation.
verification_state: Archived official source text reviewed; application to specific agencies unverified

evidence_description: Axis documentation describes scene metadata about detected objects, including people and vehicles, distributed using supported interfaces such as MQTT and RTSP. This is capability evidence, not deployment evidence.

Axis Object Track documentation describes identifiers linking detections over time and possible summaries including timestamps, classifications, speed and image snapshots. Actual NSW deployment is not established.
The NSW IPC June 2024 notice encourages agencies to consider recording AI and automated decision-making use in their Agency Information Guides to support transparency.

evidence_description: TfNSW tender WS4878301930 describes one-to-one and one-to-many facial matching and support for agency identification requests. It does not establish live CCTV matching.
